meta.title: 50 Cyber Product Ideas
meta.label: Product catalogue · Nov 2026
meta.intro: Fifty products and services that fight cybercrime, from protecting a grandmother's bank account to securing a bank's AI agents. Each one shows why it is suggested, how big the problem is, who it helps, who pays, the lowest realistic price, and how every figure was calculated.
meta.profile: a mixed-skills team selling to high-earning businesses across Pakistan, the GCC, the UK/EU and the US
meta.payNote: Mid-level to senior salary in Pakistan, plus about 25% overhead. Roughly double for a UK or Gulf team.

ideas.name: Telco Scam-Call & SMS Shield
ideas.one: Network-level detection that labels or blocks scam calls and smishing texts before they reach subscribers.
ideas.why: Most scams still start with a phone call or text. Telcos are under regulator pressure to act, and AI voice makes calls more convincing.
ideas.size: 57% of adults worldwide faced a scam attempt in a year and 23% lost money.
ideas.model: Annual licence per operator, plus per-subscriber fee at scale
ideas.mvp: Number-reputation scoring on call records and SMS content classification for one operator pilot.
ideas.comp: Hiya, TNS, Truecaller (consumer side). Few serve Pakistan and smaller GCC operators directly.
ideas.impact: Protects millions of subscribers at once, especially older and first-time internet users.
ideas.buyersText: ~25 telecom operators across Pakistan, GCC, South Asia
ideas.team: Telecom signalling engineer, ML engineer, 2 backend devs, telco sales lead
ideas.ai: High: own classifiers on call and SMS data
ideas.dependency: Operator data access and network integration
ideas.hwCost: Servers in operator data centre, $20–50k per site
ideas.legal: PTA/TDRA approval, telecom privacy rules, ISO 27001
ideas.platformRisk: Medium: Truecaller, Hiya, network equipment vendors
ideas.kill: No operator agrees to a data-sharing pilot within 120 days

ideas.name: Mule-Account Detection for Banks
ideas.one: Graph and behaviour analytics that find accounts used to receive and move scam money.
ideas.why: Every scam needs a mule account to cash out. Regulators in the UK and Pakistan are pushing banks to reimburse victims, so stopping mules saves banks money directly.
ideas.size: Investment fraud alone cost $8.65B in reported US losses in 2025. Visa paid $2.4B for BioCatch, a behavioural fraud company.
ideas.ind: Banks, microfinance banks, digital wallets, fintechs
ideas.model: Annual licence by number of accounts monitored
ideas.mvp: Batch scoring of inbound transfer patterns (fan-in, rapid pass-through, new-account velocity) on one bank's historical data.
ideas.comp: BioCatch (Visa), Featurespace (Visa), NICE Actimize. Expensive for tier-2 banks in emerging markets.
ideas.impact: Breaks the cash-out step that every scam relies on.
ideas.buyersText: ~150 banks, MFBs and wallets in Pakistan + GCC; ~300 in UK
ideas.trigger: Victim reimbursement rules (UK APP refunds, SBP liability); scam surge
ideas.team: Data scientist, 2 backend devs, fraud domain expert, bank sales lead
ideas.legal: Banking secrecy, data residency, central-bank vendor approval, ISO 27001
ideas.platformRisk: Medium: Featurespace and BioCatch (both Visa), core-banking vendors
ideas.techRisk: Labelled fraud data is scarce; false positives freeze honest accounts
ideas.kill: No bank shares historical data for a back-test within 90 days

ideas.name: SIM-Swap Risk Signal API
ideas.one: An API banks call before approving a login or transfer, returning whether the customer's SIM was recently swapped.
ideas.why: SMS one-time passwords are still the main second factor in Pakistan and much of the world. A swapped SIM gives attackers the OTP.
ideas.size: Pakistani bank customers lost over Rs10M in reported 2026 SIM-swap cases, with bank insiders involved.
ideas.buyer: Bank fraud head; telco enterprise API team
ideas.mvp: Partnership with one telco to expose SIM-change dates; bank SDK that blocks OTP delivery after a recent swap.
ideas.comp: GSMA Open Gateway, Prove, Telesign. Coverage in Pakistan and Africa is thin.
ideas.impact: Stops account takeovers that drain life savings in minutes.
ideas.buyersText: ~60 banks and wallets in Pakistan, plus partner telcos
ideas.trigger: SIM-swap losses; SBP liability on banks
ideas.team: Telco integration engineer, backend dev, partnerships lead
ideas.dependency: Critical: at least one telco must expose SIM-change data
ideas.legal: PTA approval, data-sharing agreements, privacy law
ideas.platformRisk: High: GSMA Open Gateway lets telcos sell this directly
ideas.techRisk: Telco declines or builds it itself

ideas.name: Family Scam Guard for Older Adults
ideas.one: An app plus service that screens calls, flags risky payments, and alerts a trusted family member.
ideas.why: Older people lose the most per scam and often don't report it. Families want a way to help without taking control.
ideas.size: $20.9B in reported US cybercrime losses in 2025, with older adults carrying a large share.
ideas.ind: Consumers; distributed through banks, insurers, telcos
ideas.buyer: Adult children; banks as a white-label benefit
ideas.model: Consumer subscription or B2B2C per-customer fee
ideas.mvp: Call-screening and contact allow-list app with a trusted-contact alert, plus a payment-pause tip line.
ideas.comp: Aura, Carefull, EverSafe (US only). Nothing localised for South Asia or the Gulf.
ideas.impact: Protects retirees' savings and dignity.
ideas.buyersText: Millions of consumers; ~50 banks and insurers as distributors
ideas.team: 2 mobile devs, backend dev, UX designer, growth marketer, support
ideas.ai: Medium: call and SMS classification via APIs
ideas.legal: Consumer data protection, call-recording laws, app-store review
ideas.platformRisk: High: Google, Apple and telcos add scam filters natively
ideas.techRisk: Low consumer willingness to pay; iOS restrictions

ideas.name: Deepfake-Proof Call-Centre Verification
ideas.one: Detects synthetic voices and replayed audio on bank and insurer phone lines and adds a step-up check.
ideas.why: Attackers now clone voices to pass phone-banking checks and fool help desks.
ideas.size: Vendor data puts about 1 in 15 fraud attempts as involving a deepfake, up from 0.1% three years earlier.
ideas.ind: Banking, insurance, telecom, healthcare call centres
ideas.mvp: Licensed detection model plus your orchestration layer that triggers app-push verification when risk is high.
ideas.comp: Pindrop, Reality Defender. Arabic and Urdu speech coverage is weaker.
ideas.impact: Keeps voice channels usable for customers who can't use apps.
ideas.buyersText: ~300 banks and insurers with call centres in GCC + UK
ideas.team: Audio ML engineer, backend dev, contact-centre integrator, sales lead
ideas.legal: Voice biometrics are sensitive data (GDPR, PDPL); call-recording consent
ideas.platformRisk: Medium: Pindrop; contact-centre vendors adding detection
ideas.techRisk: Detection accuracy falls as voice models improve
ideas.kill: Pilot detection under 90% at under 1% false alarms

ideas.name: Fake App & Scam-Ad Takedown
ideas.one: Finds impersonating apps, ads, social pages and domains that use a bank's or brand's name, and gets them removed.
ideas.why: Investment and shopping scams run on fake ads and lookalike apps that misuse trusted brands.
ideas.size: Shopping scams hit 54% of scam victims and investment scams 48%.
ideas.ind: Banks, brokers, e-commerce, airlines, government services
ideas.buyer: Brand protection / digital marketing head / CISO
ideas.model: Monthly subscription by number of brands and takedowns
ideas.mvp: Daily scans of app stores, Meta ad library and new domains for brand terms, plus a takedown workflow.
ideas.comp: ZeroFox, Bolster, Netcraft. Little local-language coverage.
ideas.impact: Removes the bait before people get hooked.
ideas.buyersText: ~2,000 banks, brokers, airlines and retailers across your regions
ideas.trigger: Fake ads and apps after scams make news; regulator pressure
ideas.team: Backend dev, 2 OSINT analysts, sales lead
ideas.kill: Under 5 paying brands after 90 days of outreach

ideas.name: Crypto Transaction Risk Screening
ideas.one: Wallet and transaction screening for exchanges and payment firms: sanctions, scam wallets, mixers, Travel Rule.
ideas.why: Exchanges in newly licensed markets (UAE VARA, Pakistan's crypto regulator) must screen transactions but can't afford tier-1 tools.
ideas.size: $154B flowed to illicit crypto addresses in 2025; $14–17B lost to crypto scams.
ideas.ind: Crypto exchanges, payment firms, banks with crypto desks
ideas.mvp: Screening API using public sanctions lists and community scam-wallet data, with case management.
ideas.comp: Chainalysis, TRM Labs, Elliptic. Priced for large exchanges.
ideas.impact: Makes it harder to cash out stolen and scam money.
ideas.buyersText: ~150 licensed crypto firms in UAE, Pakistan, South Asia
ideas.team: Blockchain data engineer, 2 backend devs, AML specialist
ideas.dependency: Blockchain node and data provider access
ideas.legal: AML rules, sanctions-list licensing, regulator acceptance
ideas.platformRisk: High: Chainalysis, TRM and Elliptic own the attribution data
ideas.kill: No exchange accepts it as primary or secondary screening in 90 days

ideas.name: E-commerce Fraud & COD Abuse Shield
ideas.one: Scores orders for fraud, fake cash-on-delivery orders and chargebacks for online stores.
ideas.why: Small online sellers lose margin to stolen cards, fake COD orders and refund abuse, and can't afford enterprise tools.
ideas.size: Shopping scams are the most common scam type, hitting 54% of victims.
ideas.model: Monthly plan by order volume; Shopify/WooCommerce app
ideas.mvp: Shopify/WooCommerce plug-in scoring phone, address and order history with a shared blacklist.
ideas.comp: Signifyd, Riskified (large merchants). Few tools for COD-heavy markets.
ideas.impact: Keeps small online businesses alive.
ideas.buyersText: ~50,000 online stores in Pakistan + GCC
ideas.team: 2 full-stack devs, data analyst, growth marketer
ideas.legal: Consumer data protection; rules on sharing blacklists

ideas.name: Scam Victim Recovery Concierge
ideas.one: Helps victims act in the first hours: evidence pack, bank freeze requests, police and regulator reports.
ideas.why: Victims lose time and money not knowing what to do, and fake 'recovery' firms scam them again.
ideas.size: Over 1 million complaints to the FBI's IC3 in 2025.
ideas.ind: Consumers; offered via insurers, banks, employers
ideas.buyer: Victims; insurers as an add-on benefit
ideas.model: Per case, or per-member fee via insurers
ideas.mvp: Guided web intake that produces a ready-to-send evidence pack and reports, with human case handlers.
ideas.comp: Few legitimate players; many fraudulent ones. Trust is the moat.
ideas.impact: Raises recovery rates and cuts re-victimisation.
ideas.buyersText: Consumers; ~30 insurers and employers as channels
ideas.team: Case handlers, legal adviser, web dev, marketer
ideas.legal: Cannot promise recovery; claims-management and legal-advice rules
ideas.techRisk: Trust: easily confused with recovery scams

ideas.name: Payment-Change Verification (anti-BEC)
ideas.one: Verifies every supplier bank-detail change and large payment request through an independent channel.
ideas.why: Business email compromise works by changing where invoices get paid. A verification step stops most of it.
ideas.size: BEC losses were about $3.05B in 2025 in US reports alone.
ideas.ind: Finance teams in every sector; real estate and law firms most at risk
ideas.model: Monthly subscription by number of vendors
ideas.mvp: Vendor portal that confirms bank details via verified contacts, with ERP plug-ins (Xero, QuickBooks, SAP).
ideas.comp: Eftsure, Trustpair. Little presence in the GCC and South Asia.
ideas.impact: Stops single events that can bankrupt small firms.
ideas.buyersText: ~20,000 mid-size firms in GCC, UK, Pakistan
ideas.team: 2 full-stack devs, ERP integration dev, sales lead
ideas.dependency: ERP and accounting APIs (Xero, QuickBooks, SAP, Oracle)
ideas.legal: Handles bank details: strong security and ISO 27001 expected
ideas.techRisk: Getting suppliers to use the portal

ideas.name: SaaS OAuth Exposure Monitor
ideas.one: Shows which apps, tokens and accounts can reach Salesforce, Microsoft 365 and Google data, and how to close the gaps.
ideas.why: The biggest 2026 data-theft campaign used phone calls and connected apps to drain Salesforce data from hundreds of companies.
ideas.size: The ShinyHunters campaign is linked to 40–400+ victim organisations; average breach cost is $4.99M.
ideas.ind: Retail, finance, real estate, SaaS, healthcare
ideas.mvp: Read-only connectors for Entra, Salesforce, Google and Okta; risk report with fixes.
ideas.comp: AppOmni, Obsidian, Valence. Weaker in GCC and UK upper mid-market.
ideas.impact: Protects customer records held in SaaS.
ideas.buyersText: ~1,500 Salesforce/M365-heavy firms (500+ staff) in GCC + UK
ideas.trigger: ShinyHunters breaches; Salesforce mandatory controls; NCA/SAMA access rules
ideas.team: 2 backend devs, identity security specialist, seller/founder
ideas.dependency: Salesforce AppExchange security review; Microsoft app verification
ideas.platformRisk: Medium–high: Microsoft and Salesforce native controls
ideas.kill: Fewer than 3 paid assessments from 25 conversations by day 75

ideas.name: Help-Desk Caller Verification
ideas.one: A workflow that proves a caller is the real employee before any password, MFA or payment change.
ideas.why: Help-desk impersonation was the top way in for 2026's biggest breaches.
ideas.size: Microsoft mapped a year-long vishing campaign against SaaS customers in July 2026.
ideas.ind: Any company with an IT help desk; BPOs and outsourced service desks
ideas.model: Per employee ($3–8/yr) with an annual minimum
ideas.mvp: ServiceNow/Jira plug-in with push-to-device check and manager co-approval.
ideas.comp: Nametag, Okta features. Few bundle simulation testing.
ideas.impact: Closes the most-used door into companies.
ideas.buyersText: ~3,000 firms with 1,000+ staff in UK, GCC, US
ideas.team: 2 full-stack devs, ITSM integration dev, red-team caller, sales lead
ideas.legal: Written authorisation for vishing tests; ID-verification data rules
ideas.kill: Under 3 paid simulations and 1 platform pilot in 90 days

ideas.name: Non-Human Identity & Secrets Manager
ideas.one: Finds service accounts, API keys and tokens, shows who owns them, and rotates stale ones.
ideas.why: Machines now outnumber people in most identity systems, and leaked tokens drive supply-chain attacks.
ideas.size: Cyera paid $1B for Oasis, a non-human identity company, in July 2026.
ideas.mvp: Inventory across AWS, Azure, GitHub and M365 with age, owner and usage; rotation playbooks.
ideas.comp: Oasis (Cyera), Astrix, Entro. Crowded at the top end.
ideas.impact: Shrinks the blast radius of every leaked key.
ideas.buyersText: ~2,000 cloud-heavy firms
ideas.team: 3 backend devs, cloud security engineer, sales lead

ideas.name: Passkey & Phishing-Resistant MFA Rollout
ideas.one: Tool plus service that moves banks and companies off SMS codes to passkeys and app-based approval.
ideas.why: SMS codes are defeated by SIM swaps and phishing kits; passkeys are not.
ideas.size: Pakistani banks still rely heavily on SMS one-time passwords, and SIM-swap losses keep rising.
ideas.model: Per active user, or project fee for banks
ideas.mvp: FIDO2/passkey SDK integration plus a migration playbook and user-education kit in Urdu and Arabic.
ideas.comp: Okta, Microsoft, Hypr, Transmit. Local integrators are scarce.
ideas.impact: Ends a whole class of account takeover.
ideas.buyersText: ~200 banks, wallets and government portals in Pakistan + GCC
ideas.trigger: SIM-swap fraud; regulators moving off SMS codes
ideas.team: Mobile security dev, identity architect, 2 integration engineers, project manager
ideas.dependency: Bank mobile-app teams; certified FIDO libraries
ideas.hwCost: Usually runs on the bank's own servers
ideas.platformRisk: Medium: Okta, Microsoft, global identity vendors
ideas.kill: No bank signs a paid pilot within 120 days

ideas.name: Access Review Automation
ideas.one: Automates quarterly 'who has access to what' reviews and removes leavers' access.
ideas.why: Auditors (SOX, ISO 27001, SAMA, SBP) demand access reviews; teams do them by spreadsheet.
ideas.size: Skills gaps contributed to significant incidents for almost 9 in 10 security professionals.
ideas.model: Subscription by number of apps and users
ideas.mvp: Connectors to Entra, Google, Slack and HR system; reviewer email flow; audit-ready export.
ideas.comp: SailPoint, Saviynt (enterprise), Lumos, ConductorOne.
ideas.impact: Stops ex-employees and contractors keeping access.
ideas.buyersText: ~5,000 audited mid-size firms
ideas.team: 2 full-stack devs, integration dev
ideas.platformRisk: High: SailPoint, Microsoft Entra ID Governance, many startups

ideas.name: Executive Digital Protection
ideas.one: Protects executives and their families: removes personal data online, hardens accounts, watches for deepfakes.
ideas.why: Executives are targeted for fraud, extortion and impersonation, and their families are the soft spot.
ideas.size: AI-enabled breaches were 1 in 4 malicious breaches in 2026 and cost an average $6M.
ideas.ind: Large companies, family offices, high-net-worth families
ideas.mvp: Data-broker removal, account-hardening session, dark-web and deepfake monitoring, 24/7 hotline.
ideas.comp: BlackCloak, DeleteMe. Very little in the GCC and Pakistan.
ideas.impact: Shields people who are targeted because of their role.
ideas.buyersText: ~2,000 large firms and family offices in GCC, Pakistan, UK
ideas.trigger: Deepfake fraud; extortion and kidnap risk
ideas.team: 2 OSINT analysts, device-hardening specialist, relationship manager
ideas.legal: Very sensitive personal data; strict NDAs

ideas.name: AI Agent Red-Teaming
ideas.one: Tests a company's chatbots, copilots and AI agents for prompt injection, data leaks and unsafe actions.
ideas.why: Prompt injection moved from demos to real exploitation in 2026, and boards are asking whether AI is safe.
ideas.size: Prompt injection drives most agentic-AI security failures in production.
ideas.model: Fixed-fee assessment, then a quarterly testing retainer
ideas.mvp: Test library of injection and jailbreak attacks plus a manual testing method and a board-ready report.
ideas.comp: HiddenLayer, Lakera (Check Point), big consultancies. Strong demand outstrips supply.
ideas.impact: Keeps AI from leaking customer data or being turned against its owner.
ideas.buyersText: ~1,000 enterprises deploying AI in GCC + UK
ideas.trigger: Board AI-risk questions; EU AI Act
ideas.team: 2 offensive security / AI testers, ML engineer, report writer / PM
ideas.platformRisk: Medium: automated tools from large vendors
ideas.techRisk: Techniques change fast; talent is scarce

ideas.name: Shadow-AI Usage Control
ideas.one: Browser extension that shows which AI tools staff use and stops sensitive data being pasted into them.
ideas.why: Staff paste contracts, code and customer data into public AI tools every day.
ideas.size: 1 in 4 malicious breaches were AI-enabled in 2026.
ideas.mvp: Chrome/Edge extension detecting AI sites, classifying pasted text, with block/warn policies.
ideas.comp: Harmonic, Prompt Security (SentinelOne), Netskope.
ideas.impact: Prevents accidental leaks of private data.
ideas.buyersText: ~10,000 firms with 100+ staff
ideas.team: 2 extension/full-stack devs, backend dev, marketer
ideas.platformRisk: High: Microsoft Purview, Netskope, browser vendors

ideas.name: AI Agent Permission Gateway
ideas.one: A control point between AI agents and company tools that enforces what each agent may do.
ideas.why: Agents connected to email, CRM and code can be tricked into harmful actions; few firms control those permissions.
ideas.size: Real incidents in 2026 include indirect prompt injection against agents at major platforms.
ideas.ind: Software, finance, any company deploying agents
ideas.model: Subscription by number of agents and tool calls
ideas.mvp: Proxy for MCP/tool calls with allow-lists, human approval for risky actions, and full logs.
ideas.comp: Zenity, Noma, emerging startups. Early market.
ideas.impact: Lets companies use AI agents without handing them the keys.
ideas.buyersText: ~500 firms running AI agents in production
ideas.team: 3 backend devs, AI security researcher
ideas.platformRisk: High: model vendors and cloud providers
ideas.kill: No design partner in production within 120 days

ideas.name: AI Supply-Chain Scanner
ideas.one: Scans AI models, datasets and AI libraries for malware, backdoors and malicious releases.
ideas.why: Attackers hide malware in AI packages and model files; LiteLLM was hijacked in October 2026.
ideas.size: A malicious LiteLLM release was live on PyPI on 21 Oct 2026.
ideas.ind: AI/ML teams, software companies, research labs
ideas.buyer: Head of ML platform / AppSec lead
ideas.mvp: CI plug-in that scans model files and AI dependencies against known-bad lists and risky formats.
ideas.comp: Protect AI (Palo Alto), HiddenLayer, Socket.
ideas.impact: Stops poisoned AI components entering products.
ideas.buyersText: ~3,000 ML teams
ideas.team: 2 security engineers, ML engineer
ideas.platformRisk: High: Protect AI (Palo Alto), JFrog, Socket

ideas.name: Deepfake Check for Newsrooms & Elections
ideas.one: Verification service that checks videos, images and audio for manipulation before they spread.
ideas.why: Deepfakes drive scams, election misinformation and reputational attacks, and newsrooms need fast answers.
ideas.size: Deepfakes now appear in about 1 in 15 fraud attempts (vendor data).
ideas.ind: Media, election bodies, government communications, brands
ideas.model: Subscription by checks per month; grants for civil society
ideas.mvp: Upload portal combining licensed detectors with provenance (C2PA) checks and analyst review.
ideas.comp: Reality Defender, Sensity, TrueMedia (non-profit).
ideas.impact: Protects public trust and elections.
ideas.buyersText: ~1,000 media houses, election bodies, comms teams
ideas.team: ML engineer, 2 media forensic analysts, backend dev
ideas.legal: Defamation risk if a verdict is wrong
ideas.kill: Under 5 paying or grant-funded users in 120 days

ideas.name: AI Governance Evidence Kit
ideas.one: Templates, controls and a light tool that produce ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF and EU AI Act evidence.
ideas.why: Buyers and regulators now ask companies to prove their AI is governed.
ideas.size: AI is the top skill gap in security teams (41%).
ideas.mvp: AI inventory register, risk-assessment templates, policy pack and audit checklist.
ideas.comp: Vanta/Drata add-ons, Credo AI, consultancies.
ideas.impact: Makes responsible AI practical for mid-size firms.
ideas.buyersText: ~5,000 firms needing AI evidence in UK/EU/GCC
ideas.team: AI governance consultant, content writer, web dev

ideas.name: Edge-Device Compromise Triage
ideas.one: Rapid check of VPNs, firewalls and gateways for signs of compromise after a new zero-day.
ideas.why: Patching is no longer enough; CISA now requires checks for compromise after edge zero-days.
ideas.size: 175 exploited vulnerabilities added to CISA's list Apr–Sep 2026, against 110 a year earlier.
ideas.ind: Any organisation with VPNs or firewalls; government; critical infrastructure
ideas.mvp: Per-vendor collection scripts and a 48-hour assessment report.
ideas.comp: Mandiant, large IR firms (expensive and overbooked).
ideas.impact: Finds intruders before they reach the core.
ideas.buyersText: ~3,000 organisations with edge devices in GCC/UK/Pakistan
ideas.cycle: Days in an emergency · 2–4 months for retainers
ideas.team: 2 senior DFIR analysts, tooling dev, account lead
ideas.legal: Evidence handling; liability caps in contracts

ideas.name: Attack-Surface Monitor for SMBs
ideas.one: Continuous scan of everything a small company exposes online, with fixes in plain language.
ideas.why: Exploits are now the top way into breaches, and small firms don't know what they expose.
ideas.size: Exploitation is the leading breach entry point at 31%.
ideas.ind: SMBs in every sector; MSPs reselling
ideas.mvp: Domain-based discovery, port and certificate checks, exposed-login detection, weekly email.
ideas.comp: Intruder, Detectify, UpGuard.
ideas.impact: Fixes the easiest doors for attackers.
ideas.buyersText: ~100,000 SMBs plus MSPs
ideas.team: 2 full-stack devs, security engineer, marketer

ideas.name: Exploit-Aware Patch Prioritiser
ideas.one: Tells lean IT teams which few patches to apply this week, based on what is actually being exploited.
ideas.why: Teams face thousands of vulnerabilities and can't patch them all.
ideas.size: Exploitation became the top initial-access vector in 2026 (31% of breaches).
ideas.mvp: Import scanner results, enrich with KEV and EPSS, produce a weekly 'patch these 10' list.
ideas.comp: Tenable, Rapid7, Vulcan (Tenable). Complex for small teams.
ideas.impact: Turns limited time into maximum risk reduction.
ideas.buyersText: ~20,000 IT teams
ideas.team: 2 devs, vulnerability analyst

ideas.name: Cloud Misconfiguration Checker
ideas.one: Fixed-price scans of AWS, Azure and GCP accounts for open storage, weak keys and risky settings.
ideas.why: Startups move fast in the cloud and leave data exposed.
ideas.size: Average breach cost is $4.99M, which can end a startup.
ideas.model: Monthly subscription by number of accounts
ideas.mvp: Read-only role, top 50 checks, fix-it guides, SOC 2-ready report.
ideas.comp: Wiz (Google), Orca, Prowler (open source).
ideas.impact: Prevents mass data exposure from simple mistakes.
ideas.buyersText: ~30,000 startups
ideas.team: 2 devs, cloud security engineer
ideas.platformRisk: High: Wiz free tier, Prowler, native cloud tools

ideas.name: Ransomware Recovery Testing
ideas.one: Proves backups are immutable and can actually be restored, by running real restore tests.
ideas.why: Ransomware still shuts down factories, hospitals and schools; many backups fail when needed.
ideas.size: 2026 ransomware disrupted pharma, manufacturing, transport and government in multiple regions.
ideas.mvp: Quarterly restore drill with a signed report and a gap list.
ideas.comp: Veeam, Rubrik (tools), MSPs (service).
ideas.impact: Shortens outages that stop critical services.
ideas.buyersText: ~10,000 mid-size organisations
ideas.team: 2 backup/infrastructure engineers, automation dev, account lead

ideas.name: Tamper-Proof Audit Trail
ideas.one: Copies critical logs to an independent store attackers can't edit, so investigations can be trusted.
ideas.why: State hackers used a VMware ESX zero-day in 2026 specifically to blind audit logs.
ideas.size: CISA added the ESX logging flaw to its exploited list on 28 Oct 2026.
ideas.mvp: Log forwarder with write-once storage and hash-chain integrity checks.
ideas.comp: SIEM vendors (partial), cloud object-lock.
ideas.impact: Makes it harder for attackers to cover their tracks.
ideas.buyersText: ~1,000 government, finance and infrastructure organisations
ideas.team: 2 backend devs, SOC engineer

ideas.name: Open-Source Package Firewall
ideas.one: Blocks malicious npm, PyPI and other packages before developers install them.
ideas.why: Self-spreading worms compromised hundreds of npm packages in 2026.
ideas.size: Mini Shai-Hulud alone hit 323 packages; the Red Hat npm namespace was compromised.
ideas.ind: Software companies, fintech, any team writing code
ideas.mvp: Proxy registry that checks install scripts, new maintainers and known-bad lists.
ideas.comp: Socket, Snyk, JFrog, Aikido. Crowded.
ideas.impact: Stops one bad package poisoning thousands of companies.
ideas.buyersText: ~20,000 development teams
ideas.team: 3 devs, security researcher

ideas.name: Vendor Risk Monitoring for GCC & Pakistan Banks

start: The score favours ideas that earn quickly with little cash, so the top of the ranking is mostly service-led. Use one or two of these to fund the team.

For a larger, defensible software business, look at **#10 Payment-Change Verification**, **#11 SaaS OAuth Monitor**, **#12 Help-Desk Caller Verification** and **#34 GCC Compliance Automation**. They sell to the same buyers as the service ideas, so a services-first, product-second path works: earn with assessments now, then turn repeat work into software.
caveats: Statistics come from the named reports, mostly via press coverage. Check the primary report before quoting a figure to investors.
Prices are estimates from comparable products. Validate them with 10–20 buyer conversations per idea.
Regulated ideas (fraud, telecom, child safety, insurance) need local legal advice and usually a licensed partner.
